headline: High risk of filesystem-based prompt injection and capability conflict: Gemini CLI can write/read shared files and git while social-auto-upload consumes files and broad-network APIs.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Gemini CLI can write/read the filesystem and modify git state, while social-auto-upload consumes local files for uploads. That creates a plausible shared-file injection path if Gemini writes attacker-controlled content into files B later processes. No direct parser details are documented, so I avoid high.
conditions: IF agent_a writes content into files that agent_b later reads for upload metadata or captions
IF both agents operate in the same working directory without file isolation
mitigations: Use separate working directories for each agent
Restrict agent_a to a read-only checkout when agent_b is active
Require manual review of any file agent_a creates before agent_b consumes it
Disable shared git state during paired runs
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging between producer and consumer files

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch local files in the same workspace class: Gemini CLI reads/writes repo files and cwd files, and social-auto-upload reads media/account files. If sensitive source code or account artifacts are present in the shared directory, either agent can expose them through its own network egress. The profiles do not prove default exfiltration, so medium fits.
conditions: IF sensitive source code, credentials, or account files are placed in the shared workspace
IF either agent is allowed to transmit file-derived content over its network egress
mitigations: Keep secrets outside the shared workspace
Mount only the minimum required files into each agent session
Rotate any credentials stored in cwd before paired runs
Review outbound requests from both agents during the run
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent file ACLs

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Gemini CLI has unrestricted filesystem write, shell, and git modification, while social-auto-upload also operates on files and broad network APIs. Their concurrency model says shared state is via filesystem and git only, so simultaneous writes can corrupt repo or account artifacts. Because the shared mutable surface is explicit and defaults are not isolated, high is warranted.
conditions: IF both agents run against the same repository or account-file directory
IF agent_a and agent_b modify overlapping files or git state in the same session
mitigations: Run the agents in separate clones or directories
Serialize writes with a lock file
Disable git writes for one agent during the other's run
Snapshot the workspace before starting
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination around shared files

D_cascading_error.rationale: Gemini CLI can generate code, shell commands, and file edits that social-auto-upload may then use as inputs for uploads or account actions. That creates a default pathway where B may treat A's outputs as authoritative unless the operator inserts verification. The profiles do not show explicit verification or downstream action safeguards, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF agent_b consumes files or text produced by agent_a without a verification step
IF agent_a's generated metadata, captions, or scripts are used to drive uploads
mitigations: Insert a human review step between agents
Require checksum or schema validation on A's outputs
Limit B to a dry-run mode first
Log and compare A's outputs against expected templates
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and the provided data does not show a residency, certification, or retention mismatch. Gemini CLI handles Google account login optionally and API keys; social-auto-upload handles account_name and media files. No concrete compliance breach is evidenced, so only a low residual risk remains from unspecified policies.
conditions: IF regulated data such as PHI or EU PII is placed into either agent without a matching policy
IF the operator routes the same sensitive dataset through both agents under different retention rules
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in paired runs
Confirm both tools' retention settings before use
Keep account credentials separate from content files
Document the data class allowed for each agent
requires-engineering: align residency and retention policies
